_comment: Canonical §28.4 audio settings, read by BOTH sides:
- tests/unit/control/audio-settings-ipc-contract.test.ts drives the real
adapter in src/control/services/settings-audio.ts and the real
getSettings/updateSettings in src/control/services/settings.ts;
- src-tauri/tests/ipc_contract_tests.rs drives the real Rust struct in
src-tauri/src/settings/mod.rs.
vadSensitivity is the field this fixture exists for. The slider shipped
wired to the VAD and to the Preflight meter but persisted ONLY in the
localStorage overlay: Rust's AudioSettings had no such field, toRustPatch
had no `audio` arm, so the mic tuning a presenter set for their room could
not survive a cleared browser store, and the backend billing the key could
not see the room tuning it was set to. Mapped in one direction only
is the defect this project has shipped twice; a fixture both halves read is
what makes it impossible.
0.5 is the A.6 neutral, so the value here is deliberately NOT 0.5: a field
one side maps and the other does not comes back as its default, and 0.5
would hide exactly that.
The other two fields are the rest of Rust's audio section. They are here
so the round trip is asserted on the WHOLE document rather than on one key
— a patch that silently dropped `language` would otherwise pass.
The patch the UI emits for a sensitivity change, and nothing else. The
device id and the three getUserMedia processing toggles are per-machine
capture state and stay in the overlay — a preferred device id that names
hardware another machine does not have is not a document value.
The range Rust validates, which is the range both sliders offer (0-100%
of 0-1). A value outside it is a slider that moved and clamps; a value
that is not a number at all is a document that is wrong, and falls back
to the NEUTRAL midpoint rather than to the nearest end — a corrupt
setting must not silently become the most aggressive VAD on offer.
